summary: Phase 6 (77a0659) silently redefined the Phase-5 modeled_costs_per_unit contract. Phase 5 used quote per unit (the phase5 fixtures use 1.0 at BTC 50000); Phase 6 returns a dimensionless rate sum (0.0008). This is the root regression behind F-001. Paper (fffef34) and live (7e6347a) later consumed the Phase-6 function.
expected: A function consumed across phases keeps the unit its owning phase established and tested (quote per base unit).
actual: costs.py returns fee_rate_entry + fee_rate_exit + expected_slippage, while its docstring says 'per-unit cost in quote currency ... simplified for the tracer slice'. The Phase-5 tests still pass because sizing accepts any Decimal.
impact: Origin of F-001 in backtest, paper and live. The tracer simplification was never revisited. The money consequence is counted under F-001 (P11).
evidence: tests/fixtures/phase5/happy_path_long/input.json:41 '1.0' (implied rate 2e-05); 05-CONTEXT D-01; 06-PATTERNS:359; 77a0659 costs.py:148-170; 06-01-PLAN:97 'delegating to the same per-unit formula src/risk/sizing.py consumes'; probe_costs.py -> 0.0008.
why_tests_miss: The Phase-5 parity tests inject the cost value directly. The Phase-6 parity test re-derives the rate sum by hand (06-REVIEW IN-02a). No test checks units.
recommendation: Covered by P11. Also add a contract test that modeled_costs_per_unit scales linearly with price, and fix the docstring.
known_prior: KNOWN: F-001, ROADMAP P11, 06-REVIEW IN-04/WR-13. NEW: framed as a regression of the Phase-5 contract.

summary: 06-REVIEW-FIX closed WR-03 and WR-13 as 'Opened as a cross-phase item; no code touched' and CR-04 as 'needs a design call'. No tracked item exists anywhere. The fee-unit bug stayed invisible for 3 days while paper (07-01) and live (09-01) consumed it. CR-04 (the same-bar lookahead lifecycle) is still untracked.
expected: A 'cross-phase' skip creates a STATE deferred row, backlog id or ROADMAP item in the same commit.
actual: 'cross-phase' appears only in 06 REVIEW, REVIEW-FIX and VERIFICATION. STATE.md:259-269 Deferred Items has none of the three. The first tracking is backlog 999.5 (a0ef5fc, 2026-09-29 17:40), and it covers fees only.
impact: Known HIGH defects F-001, F-901 and F-905 stayed invisible to planning. 07-REVIEW and 09-REVIEW never re-flagged modeled_costs.
evidence: 06-REVIEW-FIX WR-03/WR-13 reason text; grep -rln cross-phase .planning; STATE.md:259-269; git log -S 999.5.
reproduction: grep -rln 'cross-phase' .planning; read the STATE.md Deferred Items.
recommendation: Require a tracked id for any 'cross-phase' skip, enforced in the fixer and the disposition gate. Add backlog items for 06 CR-04 and WR-03 now.

summary: The 06 (23 fixes) and 08 (34 fixes) REVIEW-FIX waves were committed while the affected suites could not import (structlog, tenacity and the SDK were missing; system Python 3.14.3). The 'no regression' claims are vacuous. Four follow-up commits repaired tests that the 08 fixes broke, and the 06 WR-12 fix shipped with no test.
expected: Every fix is verified by the project suite in the project environment (uv/.venv, Python 3.13) before it is committed.
actual: 06: '23 passed / 13 failed ... ModuleNotFoundError structlog'; the 13 are the simulator tests. 08: 'full pytest suite could not run here ... did not block commits'. The 08 review_path is in a different OneDrive checkout.
impact: Regressions were caught only by chance, and F-804 slipped through. 06-VERIFICATION then evaluated a pre-fix view.
evidence: 06-REVIEW-FIX:23-37; 08-REVIEW-FIX:24-30; commits 8532147, db53e6b, 9048ed8, d40d1fd (23:35-23:37); 9f5a87d touches src only.
reproduction: Read the cited lines; git log --grep='^fix(0[68])' --stat.
recommendation: The fixer must refuse to commit when the in-scope suite fails to import, and must run under uv. Bisect-run the suite across the 06 and 08 fix SHAs.

summary: The 06 WR-12 review fix stamps each exit with the deciding 1m minute of the signal bar, so exit_time_utc precedes entry_time_utc (the bar close) on every 1m-resolved trade. Phase-10 compute_trade_excursion then marks each such trade INCOMPLETE NEGATIVE_INTERVAL. No test was added.
expected: exit_time_utc >= entry_time_utc for every record, asserted by a test. A review fix that changes an output field gets a regression test.
actual: Probe: intrabar_both_touched has entry 09:59:59 and exit 09:00:59 (the same for _short and limit_partial_fill). normalize_backtest + compute_trade_excursion returns NEGATIVE_INTERVAL (excursion.py:194).
impact: Backtest MFE/MAE diagnostics are empty. The red flag that would have exposed F-901 was produced on 2026-09-26 and missed.
evidence: git show 9f5a87d; src/analytics/excursion.py:192-196; probe_wr12.py, probe_excursion.py; the Phase-10 goldens are hand-written (tests/fixtures/phase10/loaders/evidence_sample.json).
why_tests_miss: 9f5a87d added no test. No test asserts entry/exit ordering. The Phase-10 fixtures are not produced by the simulator.
recommendation: Fix together with F-901. Add the ordering assertion and an integration test simulator -> normalize_backtest -> excursion.
known_prior: Root F-120/F-901. NEW: the review-fix-induced inversion and its Phase-10 consequence.

summary: 06-01 commits do not match the plan. Per-case expected.json and sha256 golden pinning (threat mitigation T-06-02) were never built. The implementation was committed before the tests and fixtures, so the RED step was not demonstrated. The no-float and mypy steps were skipped, and the planned nonzero-cost parity fixture is missing. 06-VERIFICATION still rated the suites 'Pinned ... VERIFIED'.
expected: Golden digests per case as planned (or a re-plan). Verification does not credit pinning that does not exist.
actual: The simulator case dirs contain only input.json. The test docstring claims hash equality, and _load_expected is unused. Commit order: impl 12:29:15, fixtures 12:29:31, tests 12:29:40. 06-01-SUMMARY lists a nonexistent plan 06-04.
impact: The simulator's prices, quantities, times and PnL are unpinned, so F-804 and cost changes pass silently. The stage-B claim that goldens pin the simulator bytes is inaccurate.
recommendation: Add per-case expected.json from an independent hand oracle, and add the nonzero-cost parity fixture. Correct the 'why tests miss' text of F-901/F-120.
known_prior: PARTIAL: 06-01-SUMMARY Known Limitations, 06-REVIEW IN-02(d). NEW: verification accepted it; correction to stage B.

summary: Phase-4 review fix CR-03 replaced the one-way 04-03 checkpoint decision (TP1 = minimum_rr, TP2 = entry + 2*minimum_rr*risk) with a structure-derived TP1/TP2 and moved the Family B stops. It then regenerated the phase4 goldens from the new code, all after 04-VERIFICATION had passed. STATE.md:124 and 04-03-SUMMARY still record the old rule, and the requested human verification never happened.
expected: Changing a one-way checkpoint decision re-opens it for a human, updates STATE, SUMMARY and the family sheets, and triggers re-verification.
actual: e0bde92 (2026-09-24 22:54) and 1c3c187 (2026-09-25 00:52) came after 04-VERIFICATION 6bdbe4c (22:16, status passed). 04-REVIEW-FIX:68 says 'Human verification requested' and no record of it exists.
impact: The backtest TP/SL geometry behind all family evidence was chosen by the review fixer. The human never saw it, and it contradicts the recorded decision.
reproduction: git show e0bde92 -- src/core/planner.py; git show 1c3c187 -- tests/fixtures/phase4/expected_plans.json
why_tests_miss: The goldens were regenerated from the implementation in the same wave.
recommendation: Add a DECISIONS row with a human sign-off, update STATE and the SUMMARY, and re-verify phase 04. Forbid fixture regeneration inside REVIEW-FIX for findings that request human verification.
known_prior: Related to F-113 and F-103. NEW: a decision override after verification.

summary: Beyond F-124, seven checkpoints were cleared without a recorded human decision. 03-04 (gate=blocking, one-way table shape) was auto-selected. 05-01 (gate=blocking-human, quantization semantics) was resolved '(orchestrator)'. 02-05 (human-verify, off-host backup) was resolved from the orchestrator envelope (OneDrive). 03-01, 03-02 and 07.1-01 (gate=blocking) have no resolution record. 07.1-01 offers a single option. 04-03 (one-way) was auto-selected, then overridden (F-806).
expected: Blocking, blocking-human and one-way checkpoints carry the user's verbatim answer, as 01-04 and 02-01 do.
actual: The records show auto-mode or orchestrator resolution, or nothing.
impact: The user, who delegated trading choices, never saw several irreversible choices: the DB schema, the quantization semantics and the backup target.
reproduction: grep '<task type="checkpoint' over the PLANs; read the cited SUMMARY lines.
recommendation: Present the listed decisions to the user for ratification (a DECISIONS row each). The executor should refuse gate=blocking* in auto mode, and plan-check should reject single-option decisions.
known_prior: F-124 covers 08-02, 09-01, 09-04 and 10-05; F-910/F-108 cover the backup on its merits. NEW instances.

summary: Review fix bd12652 appended atr_period and touch_tolerance_atr to the already-referenced breakout-retest and range-mr baseline-v1 sets, which changed their hashes. The only mutation tripwire (verify_parameter_set, with expected hashes held in fixtures) was satisfied by regenerating those hashes in 1c3c187. No committed hash lock exists.
expected: A new set version for semantic additions, and a committed hash lock checked in CI.
actual: parameter_set_hash changed dbcf730f->4a8ee77e and 2997f262->060fc447 in tests/fixtures/phase4/parameters.json. Nothing would stop the same edit to baseline-v3 or to a future published set.
impact: No evidence was lost then (only fixtures used v1), but the protection of published experiment identity is not enforced against committed files.
evidence: git show bd12652 -- params; git show 1c3c187 -- tests/fixtures/phase4/parameters.json; registry.py:412-444; 03-CONTEXT D-04.
why_tests_miss: The tripwire's expected values are regenerable test data.
recommendation: Add a committed params/HASHES.lock verified in CI, and forbid edits to locked sets.

WR-08 narrowed the approval-delay buckets to approvals only, dropping the OPPORTUNITY dimension named in 10-CONTEXT, without a decision record.

summary: The 07.1 test migration rewrites the 'grandfathered, byte-identical' phase-6 fixture cost dicts in memory, from partial_fill_fraction 1.0 to 0.5, so every assemble() test models half fills. It also made the Phase-5/6 canonical baseline-v2 sets unassemblable, although scripts/gen_phase6_fixtures.py:326 still targets them.
expected: A binding fix does not change the simulated economics of existing tests. A parameter change is a new, justified set version.
actual: _v3_case_input docstring: 'rebinding partial_fill_fraction from "1.0" ... to "0.5"'. 7 call sites were migrated. Commit message: 'baseline-v2 ... now raises KeyError at the gate'.
impact: Hides the F-957 behaviour change from fixture review. Phase-6 fixtures regenerated with the committed generator would be refused by assemble().
why_tests_miss: The mutation happens inside the tests.
recommendation: With F-957/P11: create a new set with partial_fill_fraction = 1, point the generator at it, and remove the in-memory rebinding.
known_prior: F-957 (the value). NEW: the test-side mechanism.
